clauses.reason: The order commands "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Auction and Loose-leaf Tobacco Warehouse Industry" under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for the Code of Fair Competition for the Auction and Loose-leaf Tobacco Warehouse Industry; the approval has legal effect only through section 3 of that title (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so the prospective operative effect of this approval ended on June 14, 1935, the date of approval, because the resolution states no later effective date. The proviso staying Section 24 of Article VII is a separate clause with its own end. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and the order states no own-terms end. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The Schechter decision of May 27, 1935 is recorded only as a validity characterization, not an end date.

later_events.mechanism: statutory_repeal_of_code_approval_and_enforcement_provisions: S.J. Res. 113 section 2, approved June 14, 1935; a later event of this clause, whose twenty-day stay had already ended by its own terms in July 1934.

clauses.reason: The proviso commands that "the provisions of Section 24 of Article VII shall not become effective, and they are hereby stayed for a period of twenty days in order to afford consideration to the objections of any interested parties, and that at the expiration of such period the provisions of such section shall become effective, unless I shall otherwise order". The stay is an own-terms fixed period: the order is dated June 30, 1934 and stays Section 24 of Article VII for "a period of twenty days", so the stay expired on July 20, 1934, twenty days after the order's date, and at the expiration of such period the section "shall become effective". The recorded date is July 20, 1934; if the day of the order is counted as the first day, the last day of the stay is July 19, 1934, and the section becomes effective the next day. The stay reserves the President's power to order otherwise, and no held order exercises it, so the stay ended before June 14, 1935 and the repeal of June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2) is a later event as to this clause.

research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6790 (signed June 30, 1934) recites the reports of the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator and five findings, then ends with one sentence that contains two operative commands: it approves the code ("do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Auction and Loose-leaf Tobacco Warehouse Industry") and it provides that "the provisions of Section 24 of Article VII shall not become effective, and they are hereby stayed for a period of twenty days in order to afford consideration to the objections of any interested parties, and that at the expiration of such period the provisions of such section shall become effective, unless I shall otherwise order". The approval depends wholly on section 3 of Title I; under the reviewed shared analysis its first end is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935), unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held. The stay of Section 24 of Article VII is a separate clause with its own fixed period of twenty days, which ended by its own terms in July 1934, before the repeal.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued, and the section 5 exemption for action completed while the code was in effect is likewise an accrued effect (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5). Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after the repeal.
